facts.label: Credit analysis
facts.text: Leverage is therefore measure-dependent. Reported EBITDA, built as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, was USD 1566.955 million for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against USD 4336.429 million on the issuer's adjusted measure. The difference of USD 2769.474 million is share-based compensation of USD 1038.104 million, contingency, restructuring and other charges of USD 1597.003 million, restructuring share-based compensation of USD 126.639 million and small items. Share-based compensation is a recurring cost the adjusted measure excludes. The charge add-back is described by the issuer as including severance, contingent losses and certain litigation and regulatory charges; the severance reserve was fully paid by September 30, 2026, while the Department of Justice accrual is unpaid, but the filing does not itemise the add-back, so its split is not established. Neither extreme is a clean read: the reported measure is depressed by charges that should not recur, and the adjusted measure is flattered by costs that are real. Basis: calculation BRIDGE-LTM; calculation LTM-EBITDA; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35, 40, 53–54

facts.label: Credit analysis
facts.text: The strongest case against a cautious reading is the balance sheet itself: cash exceeds every debt line, the revolver is undrawn and no note matures before November 2027, so debt service does not depend on either EBITDA measure in the near term. It would win if the Department of Justice payment is met from cash on hand without drawing the revolver and the restructuring charges prove one-off. The strongest case against the benign adjusted reading is the size of the add-backs relative to adjusted EBITDA; it would win if contingency charges recur in later periods or if the unpaid accrual is followed by further regulatory costs, in which case reported leverage and reported cover are the better guide. Part of the cash balance is funded by bank deposits and by customer-related float, so net cash overstates the issuer's own resources. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34–35, 55–56; calculation LEV-2026-09-30; calculation BRIDGE-LTM

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Retained consumer lending is the exposure most likely to move creditor outcomes. Loans held for investment grew 30.09% in nine months, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13% of consumer balances. Basis: calculation LOANS-20260930; calculation DELINQ-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 23, 29, 47–48

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The compliance record is a clear governance weakness. The agreement in principle with the Department of Justice rests on a deferred charge that Block failed to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, and the accrual stepped up from USD 240 million at the first quarter to USD 526 million at the second and USD 764 million at the third, against a gross monetary component of about USD 964 million, with final terms, court approval and payment timing still open. The board formed a special litigation committee in April 2026 and the derivative actions reached a settlement in principle that includes USD 150 million from insurers, so a response is visible, but it does not remove the cash call, which equals 7.59% of total liquidity at September 30, 2026. Basis: calculation DOJ-ACCRUAL; calculation DOJ-LIQ; 10-Q_2026-03-31_xyz-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_xyz-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36, 55

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The parent stands behind a regulated bank subsidiary, which adds a claim on parent liquidity. Square Financial Services must hold FDIC capital levels with a leverage ratio of at least 20%, the parent must act as a source of financial strength, and a USD 50 million reserve deposit and a third-party credit line are required; the bank began issuing brokered certificates of deposit in the third quarter, USD 381.4 million at par, all due within twelve months. In structural terms, which is this module's reading and not an issuer statement, bank depositors and certificate holders have first claim on the bank's assets, so growth in bank-funded lending moves value away from holders of the parent's notes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 56, 131

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is conduct. Block has never declared a dividend, repaid USD 1,575 million of 2026 maturities in cash without any conversion, issued no new notes in the nine months, kept the USD 900 million revolver undrawn, reports compliance with its financial covenants, and had its Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry closed in March 2026 with no enforcement action recommended. Control by the Class B holders has so far coincided with creditor-neutral or creditor-supportive actions, and the nine-month repurchase pace fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow. The issuer also states ratings of BBB- at Fitch, Ba1 at Moody's and BB+ at S&P for 2025, although no agency document is supplied. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Block runs two connected ecosystems, Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, with TIDAL and bitcoin hardware projects outside the two reportable segments, and reports revenue as Commerce enablement, Financial solutions and Bitcoin ecosystem. Gross profit is the measure management steers by, because bitcoin revenue is the price of bitcoin sold to customers and carries almost no margin. Gross profit was USD 10,359,929 thousand in FY2025 and was 24.35% higher in nine months of 2026 than a year earlier, and the base is broad: no customer exceeded 5% of Square payment volume, the United States is 91.00% of revenue and the operating record runs from 2009. The credit linkage is that processing and software income follows seller volume and gives visibility, lending income is repeat but short-dated and loss-bearing, and licences across payments, banking, lending, brokerage and bitcoin mean a regulatory action can restrict products that earn gross profit. Seasonality exists but is not quantified in the documents, with Square strongest in the fourth quarter and Cash App lifted by tax refunds in the first. Afterpay is the only acquisition the documents name, and its date and price are not stated. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Block is a listed company with no financial sponsor and concentrated voting control: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes with 9.92% of the shares, and Jack Dorsey is named as controlling shareholder for the bank regulator's purposes. The issuer of the senior notes and the convertible notes is the parent, no guarantor is named, and the debt that ranks ahead structurally sits in two places, the matched warehouse entities whose assets are not available to the parent's creditors and the bank subsidiary whose deposits and certificates rank first on its assets. Leverage tolerance is low on the evidence, with net cash, no dividends, maturities repaid from cash and no new notes in 2026, but capacity to take on debt or pay shareholders cannot be read without the executed documents. facts.label: Revenue durability
facts.text: Revenue is driven by volume and by lending volume, not by price. Square processing grew in line with payment volume, Commerce enablement revenue grew with Cash App Card and Afterpay Post-Purchase, and Financial solutions revenue grew 40.26% in nine months on Cash App Borrow, so growth is real but is increasingly lending-linked. Square sellers sign no mandatory long-term contracts, which keeps pricing transparent and lock-in low, and Cash App acquires customers through free peer-to-peer transfers, so retention rests on product use and not on contract. The credit implication is that revenue is recurring in behaviour but transactional in form, sensitive to consumer spending and credit conditions and to regulation, and bitcoin revenue, 28.33% of revenue, swings with the bitcoin price without moving gross profit much. Customer concentration is low at Square and not stated for Cash App. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 50

facts.label: Margin resilience
facts.text: Gross margin rose to 48.01% in nine months of 2026 from 41.73% because low-margin bitcoin revenue fell and higher-margin financial solutions grew, yet operating income was only 7.55% of gross profit against 16.33% a year earlier, because general and administrative expense included an increase of USD 969.2 million in litigation and regulatory accruals, a figure the Business & governance review states without saying it is the nine-month increase and not the level, and loan losses are booked at origination. Costs are part variable, with processing cost following volume and provisions following originations, and part fixed, with cloud purchase commitments of USD 2,201,264 thousand and a workforce that was cut by more than 40%. Margins can be defended against volume pressure through the cost actions, but not against a rise in loss rates, which would hit operating income before gross profit; margin stability is therefore average and depends on credit performance. Basis: calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; calculation OPMARGIN-9M2026; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 37, 45–47

Free cash flow after capital spending is a proxy only; the credit implication is that cash interest, at 9.03% of operating cash flow, is comfortably covered in the period but the quality of conversion is not established, and a cash cost of USD 764 million would absorb 26.59% of the nine-month proxy.

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense in both ecosystems, from business software providers, acquirers and banks for sellers and from money transfer apps, card issuers, brokerages and banks for consumers, and Block competes on brand, breadth and simplicity, which is not a contractual moat. The threat of new entrants is high in payments and lending because licences and data are available to well-funded fintechs, though Block's seller network and Cash App peer-to-peer network create switching effort. Substitutes include bank transfers, cards and cash, and bitcoin payment rails that Block itself promotes. Buyers have power because sellers sign no long-term contracts, and suppliers have moderate power through card networks, acquiring processors, bank partners and cloud providers whose terms set processing cost and a fixed commitment of USD 2,201,264 thousand. For creditors the forces matter through margin: rivalry limits pricing power on processing, so earnings growth must come from volume and lending, which returns the credit to loss performance. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 45

facts.text: Regulatory and economic factors are material and social and technological ones are secondary. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths that support credit are liquidity that exceeds all debt, maturities that begin in November 2027 and then in 2030, a broad seller base without concentration, a workforce cut by more than 40% and no dividend. Weaknesses that constrain credit are the gap between reported and adjusted earnings, retained consumer loans growing faster than the rest of the business, an unresolved payment of USD 764 million and concentrated voting control. Opportunities that could improve credit are gross profit growth guided at 21.87% above FY2025 for 2026, distribution expansion in Square and a final settlement at or below the accrual. Threats that could weaken credit are a consumer credit downturn, bank funding or warehouse availability tightening, regulatory conditions that limit lending, and a bitcoin price fall that cuts revenue and the USD 771.9 million investment. facts.text: Over the next 12 months to 24 months management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and at least 15% growth in 2027 with Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87% rising to 31.51%, tailwinds being Square distribution, Cash App actives and lending growth and cost savings of USD 800 million to USD 900 million a year; headwinds are the regulatory payment, higher loss provisions as lending grows, cash interest on the 2025 notes and the 2027 convertible maturity on November 1, 2027. In the medium term the senior notes, 90.04% of principal, mature in four series from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing depends on sustained earnings and on lender appetite for a business whose lending share is rising. Sector tailwinds are digital payments adoption and consumer demand for instant credit; sector headwinds are consumer credit cycles, regulation of small-dollar lending and bitcoin price swings, none of which can be quantified from the documents. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The issuer-specific downside begins with consumer credit weakening at Cash App, shown first as 60 days to 89 days past due rising beyond 4.13% and a rising allowance. The first operational break is provisioning: losses are booked at origination, so operating income falls before gross profit does, and Cash App Borrow originations may be curtailed if warehouse, deposit or brokered funding tightens or a regulator conditions the bank. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while the Department of Justice payment of about USD 764 million, taxes and any repurchases still draw cash, and reported leverage rises above 4.64x as reported EBITDA falls. Liquidity consequences stay manageable in the period: cash covers the 2027 convertible 13.67x, the revolver is undrawn and no senior note is due before 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next 12 months to 24 months; the exposures are a covenant breach that cannot be tested without the level, and a loss of bank funding that would force the parent to support the bank. Management levers are suspending repurchases, which were already nil in the third quarter, slowing originations and drawing the revolver. Observable triggers are delinquency, the allowance ratio, the final settlement terms and bank capital ratios. Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34, 56

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Block presents an adequate business profile supported by two diversified ecosystems, low customer concentration and a workforce that has been cut by more than 40%, but credit quality is constrained by retained consumer lending that is growing fast, a gap between reported and adjusted earnings and an unresolved regulatory payment. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital spending is light and operating cash flow is strong, though its quality is not established. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on loss performance, the final settlement and the covenant level, since no note matures until November 2027 and the first senior notes mature in 2030. The primary downside path is credit losses and a regulatory cash call squeezing earnings while the parent carries the lending book and supports the bank. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, loss history by cohort, stand-alone bank statements and the final settlement. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: retained consumer lending losses combined with the regulatory payment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings support a consolidated credit snapshot of Block, Inc., but creditors cannot rely on them for covenant headroom, legal priority or market pricing because no financing document, covenant level or market price is supplied.

The evidence runs from the audited 2025 annual report to the third-quarter 2026 report signed on November 3, 2026, two days before the as-of date, and it covers the 2026 note repayments, the January 2026 revolver amendment and the October 2026 agreement in principle with the Department of Justice.

Three open points limit the work: the level of the revolver's leverage covenant is printed nowhere, the Department of Justice resolution is not final and its payment timing is not stated, and governance detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

Financial foundation, Business & governance, Earnings changes, Liquidity and Fundamental credit can proceed, most with stated limitations; Legal & covenants and Market-implied risk are blocked, and Peer benchmark and Security selection are conditional on inputs the run did not supply.

spans.text: # CP-1 for Block, Inc. (xyz), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Financial foundation for Block, Inc. (issuer id xyz), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the audited fiscal 2025 and 2024 statements and the unaudited nine-month 2026 and 2025 statements, normalised on one basis, with debt, cash, liquidity and leverage measures for the latest balance-sheet date.

- Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 e2fef1f2e8cd622f6df897a62ac10760012c962b492b10cb3d5cd60b05a9546c: source gate, perimeter and gap list; the covenant level and the executed financing documents are absent.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Block's debt is serviceable, but leverage depends on which earnings measure creditors accept: 4.64x on reported EBITDA against 1.68x on the issuer's adjusted measure for the twelve months to September 30, 2026.
Basis: calculation LEV-2026-09-30; calculation LTM-EBITDA; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 50–54

The gap comes from add-backs the issuer excludes, and contingency and restructuring charges are the largest of them, ahead of share-based compensation, so part of the difference is cash that has left or is still to leave rather than an accounting item.
Basis: calculation BRIDGE-LTM; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35, 40, 53–54

Liquidity is not the constraint: cash exceeds total debt including the matched warehouse funding, which makes net debt negative on the balance sheet, and the revolver is undrawn, but the level of its leverage covenant is not disclosed, so headroom cannot be calculated.
Basis: calculation NETDEBT-2026-09-30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29, 55
### Credit analysis

Gross debt, counting every debt line on the balance sheet, fell from USD 8653.901 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 7266.567 million at September 30, 2026, because the 2026 convertible notes and the 2026 senior notes were repaid from cash and no new notes were issued, while warehouse funding rose from USD 1364.883 million to USD 1543.540 million. Cash and cash equivalents rose over the same months, so net debt moved from USD 2089.809 million to USD -592.747 million; the negative figure is net cash. The warehouse debt is matched funding of consumer receivables and loans held by separate entities whose assets are not available to the issuer's other creditors, so the notes alone, USD 5723.027 million at carrying value, are the claim that ranks against the issuer's own resources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 27–30; calculation NETDEBT-2026-09-30; calculation NETDEBT-FY2025

Leverage is therefore measure-dependent. Reported EBITDA, built as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, was USD 1566.955 million for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against USD 4336.429 million on the issuer's adjusted measure. The difference of USD 2769.474 million is share-based compensation of USD 1038.104 million, contingency, restructuring and other charges of USD 1597.003 million, restructuring share-based compensation of USD 126.639 million and small items. Share-based compensation is a recurring cost the adjusted measure excludes. The charge add-back is described by the issuer as including severance, contingent losses and certain litigation and regulatory charges; the severance reserve was fully paid by September 30, 2026, while the Department of Justice accrual is unpaid, but the filing does not itemise the add-back, so its split is not established. Neither extreme is a clean read: the reported measure is depressed by charges that should not recur, and the adjusted measure is flattered by costs that are real.
Basis: calculation BRIDGE-LTM; calculation LTM-EBITDA; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35, 40, 53–54

Interest cover shows the same split. Cash interest paid for the twelve months was USD 393.057 million against USD 246.331 million in fiscal 2025, because the senior notes issued in August 2025 carry coupons that were first paid in 2026, and cover is 3.99x on reported EBITDA against 11.03x on adjusted EBITDA. Cash interest paid may include interest on warehouse funding, which the issuer books in general and administrative expense, so the ratio is on a broader interest base than the income statement line.
Basis: calculation COVER-2026-09-30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 30, 40

Operating cash flow of USD 3001.581 million for nine months of 2026 is far above net income of USD 342.615 million, because the cash flow statement adds back transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses of USD 1687.281 million and share-based compensation of USD 871.220 million, and shows an inflow of USD 777.910 million from other assets and liabilities that the statement does not break down. Operating cash flow includes the movement in loans originally classified as held for sale and the movement in customers payable, so it is not a clean measure of cash earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

Near-term liquidity is ample against dated obligations. No note matures before the 2027 convertible notes on November 1, 2027, the warehouse facilities have USD 447.437 million falling due within a year, and the revolver is undrawn at USD 900.000 million. The claims that could draw on cash are the share repurchase programme, which absorbed USD 700.935 million in nine months, and the Department of Justice resolution accrued at USD 764.000 million with its payment date not stated.

Customers payable, a non-debt funding float, were USD 7700.091 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 6805.366 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of USD 894.725 million, partly matched on the asset side by customer funds of USD 5356.911 million. The issuer excludes customer funds from its liquidity, and this module excludes them from cash, but the obligation is repayable on demand and is the obligation most exposed to a confidence shock. Interest-bearing deposits at the bank subsidiary rose by USD 604.593 million in nine months and brokered deposits began in the third quarter; these fund cash that is counted here, which makes part of the net cash position deposit-funded.

Two events after reporting dates are kept out of period figures. The annual report records, as a subsequent event, the workforce reduction announced on February 26, 2026 with estimated charges of USD 450 million to USD 500 million, and the nine-month report shows USD 495.012 million charged; neither is in fiscal 2025 figures. The agreement in principle with the Department of Justice reached in October 2026 is accrued at September 30, 2026 but not paid, so it is not in any pro forma figure. The revolver restatement of January 14, 2026 and the repayment of the 2026 notes do not change net debt, because debt and cash fall together.

The strongest case against a cautious reading is the balance sheet itself: cash exceeds every debt line, the revolver is undrawn and no note matures before November 2027, so debt service does not depend on either EBITDA measure in the near term. It would win if the Department of Justice payment is met from cash on hand without drawing the revolver and the restructuring charges prove one-off. The strongest case against the benign adjusted reading is the size of the add-backs relative to adjusted EBITDA; it would win if contingency charges recur in later periods or if the unpaid accrual is followed by further regulatory costs, in which case reported leverage and reported cover are the better guide. Part of the cash balance is funded by bank deposits and by customer-related float, so net cash overstates the issuer's own resources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34–35, 55–56; calculation LEV-2026-09-30; calculation BRIDGE-LTM

## Gaps

- The level and definition of the maximum total net leverage ratio in the restated credit agreement are not printed in any source, so covenant headroom is not calculable for any period; this restricts every conclusion about revolver availability; severity High; the action is to obtain the restated credit agreement.

- The Department of Justice resolution is an agreement in principle accrued at USD 764.000 million at September 30, 2026 with no final agreement, payment amount, schedule or funding source stated, so no pro forma net debt can be built and the timing of the cash outflow against liquidity is not established; severity High; the action is to update the figures when the agreement is signed.

- No balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is in the sources, so the nine months 2025 column of the balance sheet is not supplied and interim leverage is stated for September 30, 2026 only; severity Medium; the action is to add the third-quarter 2025 report.

- Assets by reportable segment are not presented and no stand-alone parent or bank-subsidiary statements are supplied, so corporate cash and debt cannot be separated from bank, customer-funds and warehouse items except through the notes; severity Medium; the action is to request segment assets and parent-only data.

- No borrower scope, guarantor or restricted group is named for the notes, the revolver or the warehouse facilities, so the obligor scope in the debt stack states only the Company and the warehouse special-purpose entities; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures and the credit agreement.

- The balance sheet lines the third-quarter report folds into other lines (property and equipment, long-term debt securities, operating lease assets, deferred tax liabilities and operating lease liabilities) are not supplied for September 30, 2026, and short-term investments are not shown separately; severity Low; the action is to use the quarterly balance sheet detail if filed.

- Cash flow statement dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero: proceeds from senior notes in nine months 2026, repayments of senior notes in the earlier columns, convertible note redemptions in FY2024, and the goodwill and intangible impairment add-back in FY2025 and both nine-month periods; the current portion of long-term debt at September 30, 2026 is read as nil because the notes table total equals long-term debt; severity Low; no action beyond the filings.

- Discrete quarterly cash flows are not printed, only cumulative figures, so no third-quarter 2026 or 2025 cash flow column is built; a third-quarter column could be derived as nine months less six months from the second-quarter report if discrete quarters are needed; severity Low.

- The floor and margin of the revolver and warehouse facilities, the commitment of each warehouse facility (only an aggregate printed as USD 2.4 billion) and the definition of liquidity in the revolver maturity test are not printed; severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement and facility documents.

- Whether cash interest paid includes interest on the warehouse facilities is not stated, so interest cover is on an interest base of uncertain breadth; severity Low; the action is to confirm with the issuer.

- Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA; share-based compensation is not added back, so reported EBITDA is conservative against the issuer's measure; severity Low; the action is none, both measures are shown.
- Warehouse availability at December 31, 2024 is not printed, so the FY2024 liquidity row excludes it; severity Low; the action is none.

## Request

Business and governance review of Block, Inc. (issuer id xyz), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions, dated history and governance and capital-allocation behaviour, from the seven supplied files and the Source readiness review.
## Sources

- Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 e2fef1f2e8cd622f6df897a62ac10760012c962b492b10cb3d5cd60b05a9546c: source gate, perimeter and gap list; the proxy statement, the executed financing documents and the covenant level are absent.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Block carries medium governance and sponsor risk for creditors: there is no financial sponsor to support them, a Class B holder group casting 52.41% of the votes decides stockholder matters, and protection rests on the issuer's own cash and covenants.
Basis: calculation VOTE-20261030; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 138; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

The exposure that matters most is Cash App lending, where loan losses rose 167.78% in nine months, while bitcoin supplies 28.33% of revenue but only 2.07% of gross profit. Creditors hold notes of USD 5,775 million whose indentures, as the issuer summarises the 2030, 2032 and 2033 series, limit liens, certain subsidiary debt, sale-leasebacks and asset transfers, and a USD 764 million regulatory accrual has no stated payment date.

Basis: calculation LOSS-9M2026; calculation REVMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation PRINC-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 189, 191
### Key findings

Control sits with a Class B holder group and not with a sponsor, and its vote far exceeds its economic stake: Class B shares are 9.92% of shares outstanding but cast 52.41% of the votes, so Class B holders can approve or block any matter put to stockholders. The issuer names Jack Dorsey as the controlling shareholder for the bank regulator's purposes and says the Class B group includes executive officers, employees and directors, but the proxy statement that would name holders and stakes is not supplied. No equity injection, cure, dividend recapitalisation, sponsor fee or related financing appears in any supplied document, so willingness to support creditors has not been tested either way.
Basis: calculation VOTE-20261030; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 99, 214; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 138

Shareholder returns are large but cash-funded and slowing: repurchases were 23.35% of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 against 78.65% a year earlier, no dividend has ever been declared, and no shares were repurchased in the third quarter, with USD 4.6 billion of the USD 9 billion authorization still available. The program is discretionary and can resume at any time, so it is capacity for cash leakage rather than a commitment, and the credit agreement's customary limits on dividends and repurchases are the only brake the supplied documents describe, at a level not printed.

Basis: calculation BBOCF-9M2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2025; calculation BBPROG-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 31, 43, 143; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71, 107

Gross profit is concentrated in Cash App and in lending-linked products: Cash App supplied 63.92% of nine-month 2026 gross profit and Square 35.43%, and the Financial solutions line, which carries the lending, supplied 41.39% of gross profit against 36.13% a year earlier. Square gives a steadier base, because no customer exceeded 5% of Square payment volume in 2025, 2024 or 2023, but Square gross profit grew 12.11% against 32.11% for Cash App, so the faster-growing franchise also carries most of the retained loan book, 78.22% of loans held for investment at amortized cost.

Basis: calculation SEGGP-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2025; calculation SEGGP-GROWTH; calculation LOANMIX-20260930; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19, 39

Retained consumer lending is the exposure most likely to move creditor outcomes. Loans held for investment grew 30.09% in nine months, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13% of consumer balances. The issuer says underlying loss rates are stable and the reserve build shows provisioning ahead of growth, but the delinquency movement is the first signal to watch because the retained book sits on the balance sheet and is part-funded by bank deposits, brokered certificates and the warehouse lines.
Basis: calculation LOANS-20260930; calculation DELINQ-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 23, 29, 47–48

Bitcoin inflates revenue without adding to creditor cash flow: it supplied 28.33% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 2.07% of gross profit, against 36.35% and 4.02% a year earlier, so revenue-based scale measures overstate the business and understate the weight of lending. Block also holds a long-term bitcoin investment valued at USD 771.9 million whose fair-value changes run through net income, with a loss of USD 31.6 million in the nine months, which adds earnings volatility that is not operating cash.
Basis: calculation REVMIX-9M2026; calculation REVMIX-9M2025; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2025; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 49, 56

The compliance record is a clear governance weakness. The agreement in principle with the Department of Justice rests on a deferred charge that Block failed to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, and the accrual stepped up from USD 240 million at the first quarter to USD 526 million at the second and USD 764 million at the third, against a gross monetary component of about USD 964 million, with final terms, court approval and payment timing still open. The board formed a special litigation committee in April 2026 and the derivative actions reached a settlement in principle that includes USD 150 million from insurers, so a response is visible, but it does not remove the cash call, which equals 7.59% of total liquidity at September 30, 2026.

The parent stands behind a regulated bank subsidiary, which adds a claim on parent liquidity. Square Financial Services must hold FDIC capital levels with a leverage ratio of at least 20%, the parent must act as a source of financial strength, and a USD 50 million reserve deposit and a third-party credit line are required; the bank began issuing brokered certificates of deposit in the third quarter, USD 381.4 million at par, all due within twelve months. In structural terms, which is this module's reading and not an issuer statement, bank depositors and certificate holders have first claim on the bank's assets, so growth in bank-funded lending moves value away from holders of the parent's notes.

Cost actions are real but management-estimated: the workforce fell by more than 40%, charges of USD 495.0 million fell inside the estimate of USD 450 million to USD 500 million, and annualised savings of USD 800 million to USD 900 million are management's figure, partly reinvested, with no independent measure supplied. The savings have not yet shown in reported operating income, because general and administrative expense rose 70% in nine months on litigation and regulatory accruals.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is conduct. Block has never declared a dividend, repaid USD 1,575 million of 2026 maturities in cash without any conversion, issued no new notes in the nine months, kept the USD 900 million revolver undrawn, reports compliance with its financial covenants, and had its Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry closed in March 2026 with no enforcement action recommended. Control by the Class B holders has so far coincided with creditor-neutral or creditor-supportive actions, and the nine-month repurchase pace fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow. The issuer also states ratings of BBB- at Fitch, Ba1 at Moody's and BB+ at S&P for 2025, although no agency document is supplied.
Basis: calculation REPAY-2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2025; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 34, 58

The view would turn adverse on a debt-funded distribution or repurchase while the Department of Justice payment is outstanding, a final settlement above the USD 764 million accrued or with operating restrictions, consumer delinquency moving beyond the 4.13% now reported, a leverage covenant level that leaves little headroom once disclosed, a use of the Class B vote to change the capital structure or related-party dealings, or parent cash committed to the bank subsidiary beyond the USD 50 million reserve. It would improve if the proxy statement showed board-level control of capital allocation that is independent of the Class B holders and if the final settlement matched the accrual.

### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so named holders, Class B holdings by holder, director independence, committee membership and executive pay are not established; the control conclusion rests on the issuer's aggregate voting statement and cannot say who would act or how.

- The indentures and the restated credit agreement are not supplied, so limits on shareholder payments, investments and new debt are read only from the issuer's summaries; the conclusion on protection against value extraction is a statement of unknown capacity, not of limited capacity.

- No dates, prices or funding for the Afterpay acquisition are supplied and TIDAL has no acquisition history, so the view on acquisition appetite rests on the absence of any material acquisition in 2025 and 2026 and not on a funding history.

- Customer and activity counts are management's unaudited measures given only for December 2025 and September 2026, so operating durability is judged on reported direction and not on cohort or retention data.

- The Department of Justice resolution is an agreement in principle, so the USD 764 million accrual may change and its effect on liquidity cannot be timed; the governance conclusion on compliance is provisional until the final agreement is signed.
- No market, peer or rating-agency document is supplied, so how lenders price governance and control is not assessed and the stated ratings rest on the issuer's own statement.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No material acquisition, disposal, merger or sponsor transaction is announced or completed in the supplied documents for 2025 or the first nine months of 2026; acquired intangible assets added were USD 5,217 thousand in FY2025 and nothing in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The transactions that matter to creditors are financing, capital-return and settlement events. New debt in the last three years: USD 2.0 billion of 6.50% senior unsecured notes due May 15, 2032, issued May 9, 2024, and USD 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes issued August 18, 2025, of which USD 1.2 billion bear 5.625% and mature August 15, 2030 and USD 1.0 billion bear 6.000% and mature August 15, 2033, with issuance costs of USD 28.3 million. Overall, Block presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is cash-funded repurchases under Class B voting control, which matters because cash can leave outside creditor control and implies a sensitivity to the Department of Justice payment. Countervailing evidence is that no dividend, sponsor fee, liability-management transaction or debt-funded distribution is documented. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed financing documents and the final agreement with the Department of Justice.

spans.text: # CP-2 for Block, Inc. (xyz), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Block, Inc. (issuer id xyz), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business quality, financial profile, liquidity, refinancing capacity, governance, downside path and monitoring triggers, drawing on the seven supplied files and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance reviews.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1, Q3 2026 shareholder letter | not stated | a2c931043c84d33fdc40710a24c2e84aa25d66394cc76e294f6f9e8221b76b85 | Guidance for 2026 and outlook for 2027 and activity counts, labelled as management language |
- Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 e2fef1f2e8cd622f6df897a62ac10760012c962b492b10cb3d5cd60b05a9546c: source gate, perimeter and gap list.

- Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 b47a7cd902509115a36c58582c00de8a4ac740511c51c94babf37260fad597e2: debt, cash, EBITDA on reported and adjusted measures, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities.
- Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 9deb34fb090ff53e265083b2785117306eccbb65c85cec2437cb5adda5a906fb: ownership, control, transactions, operating model, behaviour flags and gaps.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Block presents an adequate fundamental credit profile that rests on liquidity and low near-term maturities rather than on clean earnings: cash exceeds all debt, but leverage depends on the earnings measure, lending exposure is growing quickly and a regulatory payment is unresolved.
Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Total debt is 4.64x reported EBITDA but 1.68x the issuer's adjusted measure, net cash equals 0.38x reported EBITDA, issuer-stated liquidity is USD 10.1 billion and the next note maturity is the USD 575 million 2027 convertible. The primary downside path is a credit-loss and regulatory cash squeeze on a lending book that the parent carries on its own balance sheet.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 55
### Key findings

Liquidity is the strongest support and does most of the work: cash and cash equivalents cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x, issuer-stated total liquidity covers the notes principal 1.74x, the USD 900 million revolver is undrawn, no senior note falls due before 2030, and 90.04% of the notes principal falls due in four series from 2030 to 2033. Part of the cash is deposit-funded and customer-related float is large, so the cushion is real but not all of it is the issuer's own money.
Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27–28, 55–56

Leverage is measure-dependent, so no single ratio settles the credit: total debt is 4.64x reported EBITDA and 1.68x adjusted EBITDA, notes alone are 3.65x and 1.32x, and interest cover is 3.99x reported against 11.03x adjusted. The add-backs are 63.87% of adjusted EBITDA and include the contingency and restructuring charges that are partly cash, so the reported figures are the safer guide until the regulatory matter is settled.
Basis: calculation NOTESLEV-20260930; calculation ADDBACK-LTM; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Cash flow is strong but not clean: operating cash flow in nine months of 2026 was 53.24% higher than a year earlier and purchases of property and equipment were only 4.26% of it, leaving a proxy of USD 2,873,585 thousand, yet the figure includes movements in loans and customer balances and an unexplained inflow in other assets and liabilities. Light capital intensity gives flexibility, but conversion of earnings to free cash is not established.
Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

Retained consumer lending is the main credit-quality exposure: loans held for investment grew 30.09%, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, loan losses rose 167.78% and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13%. Losses are provisioned at origination, so growth depresses reported operating income first, and nine-month operating income was 42.49% lower even as gross profit grew; the loan book is therefore both the growth engine and the first place stress would show.
Basis: calculation OPINC-9M2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19–20, 47–48

The unresolved Department of Justice matter is the largest quantified contingent claim on cash: the accrual of USD 764 million equals 48.76% of reported EBITDA and 9.72% of cash, with final terms, court approval and payment timing not stated and losses above the accrual reasonably possible. It is affordable from cash on hand, which is why it is a constraint on the profile and not a threat to liquidity, but it would be less comfortable if paid while repurchases resumed.
Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

Control and financial policy are adequate but unproven: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes, no dividend has ever been declared, repurchases fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow and no notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026, yet the leverage covenant level is not printed and capacity to extract value is unknown without the executed documents. Governance is a medium risk rather than a strength.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 28, 31, 138

Gross profit growth supports deleveraging if it persists: management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and an Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87%, and nine-month gross margin rose to 48.01% from 41.73% as low-margin bitcoin revenue fell. The guidance is not reconciled to GAAP, so it frames the outlook and does not prove it.
Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger view is the balance sheet: cash exceeds every debt line, net cash equals 0.38x reported EBITDA, no note falls due before November 2027 and the issuer states an investment-grade rating from Fitch of BBB-. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is the pace of retained lending, where loan losses rose 167.78% in nine months while nine-month operating income fell 42.49%, and an unresolved payment equal to 48.76% of reported EBITDA. The adequate view holds because liquidity absorbs the payment and the lending growth is, on the issuer's account, matched by stable loss rates.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34–35, 47–48, 58

The view would move up if the final settlement matched the accrual and was paid from cash, the executed credit agreement showed ample headroom under the net leverage test, and delinquency stopped rising. It would move down if consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due kept rising beyond 4.13%, if the final settlement exceeded the accrual or brought operating conditions, if repurchases resumed at the pace of 2025, or if bank funding or warehouse availability tightened while originations kept growing.
Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 29–30, 34–35, 56
### Limitations

- The level and definition of the maximum total net leverage covenant are not printed, so headroom, and with it the reliability of the revolver as a backstop in a stress, cannot be assessed; the liquidity conclusion assumes the facility stays available.

- Reported EBITDA is built from operating income and depreciation because the issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so every leverage and cover conclusion carries a range between the two measures and not a single reading.

- No peer figures, traded prices or agency reports are supplied, so the view that the profile is adequate is absolute and not relative, and market access is judged from a 2025 issue and the issuer's own ratings statement.

- No stand-alone parent or bank subsidiary statements are supplied, so the split of cash and funding between the corporate group, the bank and customer-related float rests on notes, and the net cash conclusion could be overstated by deposit-funded cash.

- Loss history by origination cohort is not supplied for consumer lending, so the conclusion on credit quality rests on reserve ratios and delinquency movements over two dates and cannot separate growth effects from deterioration.

- Management guidance is non-GAAP and carries no cash flow, capital spending or debt service guidance, so the outlook conclusions describe earnings direction only and give no forward view of free cash flow.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Liquidity and net cash are the first strength. Cash and cash equivalents exceed all debt including matched warehouse funding, cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x and sit beside an undrawn USD 900 million revolver, which means maturities and the regulatory payment can be met from cash without market access in the next 12 months to 24 months.
Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 55

A distant and ladder-like maturity profile is the second strength. The first note maturity is the USD 575 million convertible on November 1, 2027 and the senior notes mature from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing pressure arrives later, which gives time for the regulatory matter to be settled and for the lending cycle to show its credit performance.
Basis: calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Scale and diversification across two ecosystems are the third strength. Two reportable segments, three revenue lines, no customer above 5% of Square payment volume and Square processing revenue that grew in line with payment volume give gross profit a broader base than a single product, which supports cash-flow visibility.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 44

Cash-funded capital policy is the fourth strength. No dividend has ever been declared, the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575 million were repaid from cash and repurchases fell sharply as a share of operating cash flow, so leverage has not been raised to fund shareholder returns.
Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; calculation REPAY-2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27

Measure-dependent earnings are the first weakness. Reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA differ by add-backs equal to 63.87% of the adjusted figure, and reported operating income fell 42.49% in nine months, so lenders cannot rely on the adjusted measure for debt service capacity.
Basis: calculation ADDBACK-LTM; calculation OPINC-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 53–54

Retained consumer lending credit risk is the second weakness. Loans held for investment grew 30.09%, loan losses rose 167.78% and early delinquency rose, so a downturn in consumer credit would reduce operating cash flow and use balance sheet funding at the same time.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 47–48

The regulatory payment is the third weakness. An accrual of USD 764 million, equal to 48.76% of reported EBITDA, has no stated payment date, and the deferred charge concerns anti-money-laundering controls that also matter to the bank subsidiary's standing.
Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

Concentrated control and discretionary repurchases are the fourth weakness. A Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes and the repurchase program has USD 4.6 billion of authorization left, so cash can be redirected to equity holders by a board elected under that control.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 138

Opaque covenant and bank perimeter are the fifth weakness. The leverage covenant level is not printed and the parent must support a bank subsidiary that funds lending with deposits and brokered certificates, so headroom and the claims ranking ahead of note holders cannot be measured.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 56
### Confidence inputs
| Input | Value |

### Company description

Block runs two connected ecosystems, Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, with TIDAL and bitcoin hardware projects outside the two reportable segments, and reports revenue as Commerce enablement, Financial solutions and Bitcoin ecosystem. Gross profit is the measure management steers by, because bitcoin revenue is the price of bitcoin sold to customers and carries almost no margin. Gross profit was USD 10,359,929 thousand in FY2025 and was 24.35% higher in nine months of 2026 than a year earlier, and the base is broad: no customer exceeded 5% of Square payment volume, the United States is 91.00% of revenue and the operating record runs from 2009.

The credit linkage is that processing and software income follows seller volume and gives visibility, lending income is repeat but short-dated and loss-bearing, and licences across payments, banking, lending, brokerage and bitcoin mean a regulatory action can restrict products that earn gross profit. Seasonality exists but is not quantified in the documents, with Square strongest in the fourth quarter and Cash App lifted by tax refunds in the first. Afterpay is the only acquisition the documents name, and its date and price are not stated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 21–24, 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 39
### Ownership and group structure

Block is a listed company with no financial sponsor and concentrated voting control: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes with 9.92% of the shares, and Jack Dorsey is named as controlling shareholder for the bank regulator's purposes. The issuer of the senior notes and the convertible notes is the parent, no guarantor is named, and the debt that ranks ahead structurally sits in two places, the matched warehouse entities whose assets are not available to the parent's creditors and the bank subsidiary whose deposits and certificates rank first on its assets.

Leverage tolerance is low on the evidence, with net cash, no dividends, maturities repaid from cash and no new notes in 2026, but capacity to take on debt or pay shareholders cannot be read without the executed documents. Governance is a medium risk because control is concentrated, the compliance record led to a deferred charge and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92, 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 138
### Revenue durability

Revenue is driven by volume and by lending volume, not by price. Square processing grew in line with payment volume, Commerce enablement revenue grew with Cash App Card and Afterpay Post-Purchase, and Financial solutions revenue grew 40.26% in nine months on Cash App Borrow, so growth is real but is increasingly lending-linked. Square sellers sign no mandatory long-term contracts, which keeps pricing transparent and lock-in low, and Cash App acquires customers through free peer-to-peer transfers, so retention rests on product use and not on contract.

The credit implication is that revenue is recurring in behaviour but transactional in form, sensitive to consumer spending and credit conditions and to regulation, and bitcoin revenue, 28.33% of revenue, swings with the bitcoin price without moving gross profit much. Customer concentration is low at Square and not stated for Cash App.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 50
### Margin resilience

Gross margin rose to 48.01% in nine months of 2026 from 41.73% because low-margin bitcoin revenue fell and higher-margin financial solutions grew, yet operating income was only 7.55% of gross profit against 16.33% a year earlier, because general and administrative expense included an increase of USD 969.2 million in litigation and regulatory accruals, a figure the Business & governance review states without saying it is the nine-month increase and not the level, and loan losses are booked at origination. Costs are part variable, with processing cost following volume and provisions following originations, and part fixed, with cloud purchase commitments of USD 2,201,264 thousand and a workforce that was cut by more than 40%.

Margins can be defended against volume pressure through the cost actions, but not against a rise in loss rates, which would hit operating income before gross profit; margin stability is therefore average and depends on credit performance.
Basis: calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; calculation OPMARGIN-9M2026; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 37, 45–47
### Cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is low: purchases of property and equipment were USD 127,996 thousand in nine months of 2026, 4.26% of operating cash flow, and cash paid for interest was USD 270,946 thousand against USD 124,220 thousand a year earlier as the 2025 notes began paying coupons. Operating cash flow of USD 3,001,581 thousand benefits from add-backs of loan losses and share-based compensation and from movements in loans and customers payable, and cash taxes of USD 194,555 thousand and the accrued regulatory payment are still to be absorbed.

Free cash flow after capital spending is a proxy only; the credit implication is that cash interest, at 9.03% of operating cash flow, is comfortably covered in the period but the quality of conversion is not established, and a cash cost of USD 764 million would absorb 26.59% of the nine-month proxy.
Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; calculation INTEREST-OCF; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 34, 40
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense in both ecosystems, from business software providers, acquirers and banks for sellers and from money transfer apps, card issuers, brokerages and banks for consumers, and Block competes on brand, breadth and simplicity, which is not a contractual moat. The threat of new entrants is high in payments and lending because licences and data are available to well-funded fintechs, though Block's seller network and Cash App peer-to-peer network create switching effort. Substitutes include bank transfers, cards and cash, and bitcoin payment rails that Block itself promotes. Buyers have power because sellers sign no long-term contracts, and suppliers have moderate power through card networks, acquiring processors, bank partners and cloud providers whose terms set processing cost and a fixed commitment of USD 2,201,264 thousand.
For creditors the forces matter through margin: rivalry limits pricing power on processing, so earnings growth must come from volume and lending, which returns the credit to loss performance.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 45
### Macro and regulatory factors

Regulatory and economic factors are material and social and technological ones are secondary. The deferred anti-money-laundering charge, bank-regulator conditions on Square Financial Services and state and federal lending and money transmission licences make regulation a direct driver of cash and permitted products, and consumer credit conditions and the bitcoin price drive loan losses and revenue. Artificial intelligence is credited by management for lower cost and faster product release, but its effect on credit is only the cost savings already estimated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 91–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 43
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths that support credit are liquidity that exceeds all debt, maturities that begin in November 2027 and then in 2030, a broad seller base without concentration, a workforce cut by more than 40% and no dividend. Weaknesses that constrain credit are the gap between reported and adjusted earnings, retained consumer loans growing faster than the rest of the business, an unresolved payment of USD 764 million and concentrated voting control. Opportunities that could improve credit are gross profit growth guided at 21.87% above FY2025 for 2026, distribution expansion in Square and a final settlement at or below the accrual. Threats that could weaken credit are a consumer credit downturn, bank funding or warehouse availability tightening, regulatory conditions that limit lending, and a bitcoin price fall that cuts revenue and the USD 771.9 million investment.

Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 56

### Outlook

Over the next 12 months to 24 months management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and at least 15% growth in 2027 with Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87% rising to 31.51%, tailwinds being Square distribution, Cash App actives and lending growth and cost savings of USD 800 million to USD 900 million a year; headwinds are the regulatory payment, higher loss provisions as lending grows, cash interest on the 2025 notes and the 2027 convertible maturity on November 1, 2027. In the medium term the senior notes, 90.04% of principal, mature in four series from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing depends on sustained earnings and on lender appetite for a business whose lending share is rising.

Sector tailwinds are digital payments adoption and consumer demand for instant credit; sector headwinds are consumer credit cycles, regulation of small-dollar lending and bitcoin price swings, none of which can be quantified from the documents.
Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; calculation WALL-2030-2033; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 34, 43
### Downside scenario

The issuer-specific downside begins with consumer credit weakening at Cash App, shown first as 60 days to 89 days past due rising beyond 4.13% and a rising allowance. The first operational break is provisioning: losses are booked at origination, so operating income falls before gross profit does, and Cash App Borrow originations may be curtailed if warehouse, deposit or brokered funding tightens or a regulator conditions the bank. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while the Department of Justice payment of about USD 764 million, taxes and any repurchases still draw cash, and reported leverage rises above 4.64x as reported EBITDA falls.

Liquidity consequences stay manageable in the period: cash covers the 2027 convertible 13.67x, the revolver is undrawn and no senior note is due before 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next 12 months to 24 months; the exposures are a covenant breach that cannot be tested without the level, and a loss of bank funding that would force the parent to support the bank. Management levers are suspending repurchases, which were already nil in the third quarter, slowing originations and drawing the revolver. Observable triggers are delinquency, the allowance ratio, the final settlement terms and bank capital ratios.
Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34, 56
### Overall credit view

Overall, Block presents an adequate business profile supported by two diversified ecosystems, low customer concentration and a workforce that has been cut by more than 40%, but credit quality is constrained by retained consumer lending that is growing fast, a gap between reported and adjusted earnings and an unresolved regulatory payment. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital spending is light and operating cash flow is strong, though its quality is not established. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on loss performance, the final settlement and the covenant level, since no note matures until November 2027 and the first senior notes mature in 2030. The primary downside path is credit losses and a regulatory cash call squeezing earnings while the parent carries the lending book and supports the bank. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, loss history by cohort, stand-alone bank statements and the final settlement.
Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: retained consumer lending losses combined with the regulatory payment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34

## Gaps
| Gap | What is missing | Why it matters | Effect on this run | Remediation |

| Covenant level (material) | The maximum total net leverage level, its definition and the headroom | The revolver is the stated backstop and its availability in a stress cannot be tested | Liquidity and refinancing conclusions assume the facility stays available | Supply the restated credit agreement |

| Department of Justice final terms (material) | Final agreement, court approval, payment schedule and funding source | Sizes and times a cash call of 48.76% of reported EBITDA and any operating conditions | The USD 764 million accrual is used and terms above it are not modelled | Update when the agreement is signed |

| Loss history by cohort (minor) | Origination cohort losses and delinquency roll rates for Cash App Borrow and Afterpay products | Separates growth from deterioration in the retained book | Credit quality is read from reserve ratios and two delinquency dates | Request cohort data from the issuer |

| Peers, prices and agency reports (minor) | Peer figures, traded prices and rating agency reports | Relative strength and market access cannot be judged | The profile is assessed on an absolute basis only | Supply peer and market data |

| Stand-alone parent and bank statements (minor) | Parent-only and Square Financial Services statements and capital ratios | Separates corporate cash from bank and customer-related float and sizes the support obligation | Net cash is read on the consolidated balance sheet | Request bank filings |
